explanation: As per the rules governing CERSAI under the SARFAESI Act, particulars of the creation of security interest must be registered within 30 days of such creation.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Under the RBI regulatory framework for digital lending, borrowers must be provided with a look-up/cool-off period during which they can exit the digital loan without penalty. Who bears the cost if the borrower exits during this window?
audio_script: Under the RBI regulatory framework for digital lending, borrowers must be provided with a look-up/cool-off period during which they can exit the digital loan without penalty. Who bears the cost if the borrower exits during this window?
option_a: The borrower must pay a standard administrative fee.
option_b: The Regulated Entity bears the proportional interest and penal charges for the days.
option_c: The borrower shall be refunded the principal and proportionate APR without any penalty, provided they return the principal within the cool-off period.
option_d: The Lending Service Provider must absorb all credit risk indefinitely.
explanation: Regulated Entities must provide a cool-off/look-up period during which borrowers can exit digital loans by paying the principal and proportionate APR without any penalty.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: According to RBI guidelines on asset classification, a term loan account is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) if interest or principal installment remains overdue for a period exceeding how many days?
audio_script: According to RBI guidelines on asset classification, a term loan account is classified as a Non-Performing Asset if interest or principal installment remains overdue for a period exceeding how many days?
option_a: 30 days
option_b: 60 days
option_c: 90 days
option_d: 180 days
explanation: As per RBI prudential norms on Income Recognition and Asset Classification (IRAC), an account becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) if interest or principal installment remains overdue for more than 90 days in respect of a term loan.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: In the context of continuous credit underwriting requirements for Regulated Entities (REs) utilizing First Loss Default Guarantee (FLDG) structures with Lending Service Providers (LSPs), within how many days must an RE invoke the FLDG upon a borrower defaulting on a loan repayment, and can the RE outsource the core credit underwriting decision to the LSP?
audio_script: In the context of continuous credit underwriting requirements for Regulated Entities utilizing First Loss Default Guarantee structures with Lending Service Providers, within how many days must an RE invoke the FLDG upon a borrower defaulting on a loan repayment, and can the RE outsource the core credit underwriting decision to the LSP?
option_a: Within 30 days of default; yes, LSPs can take standalone credit decisions
option_b: Within 120 days of default; no, REs cannot outsource the core credit underwriting decision and must invoke FLDG within a maximum overdue of 90 days or asset classification as NPA, whichever is earlier
option_c: Within 90 days or when the account is classified as NPA, whichever is earlier; no, REs must retain ultimate responsibility for credit underwriting and cannot outsource it to the LSP
option_d: Within 180 days of default; yes, if backed by 100% cash collateral
explanation: As per RBI digital lending frameworks, REs cannot pass on the credit underwriting responsibility or make credit decisions independently outsourced to LSPs. Furthermore, invocation of FLDG must occur within a maximum overdue of 90 days, or when the account is classified as Non-Performing Asset (NPA), whichever is earlier, to maintain transparency and robust credit risk management.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: In the context of debt recovery and guarantees, what specific right does a surety acquire under Section 140 of the Indian Contract Act upon paying off the guaranteed debt when the principal debtor defaults?
audio_script: In the context of debt recovery and guarantees, what specific right does a surety acquire under Section 140 of the Indian Contract Act upon paying off the guaranteed debt when the principal debtor defaults?
option_a: Right of subrogation, stepping into the shoes of the creditor
option_b: Right to take over management of the creditor's bank
option_c: Right to imprison the principal debtor independently
option_d: Right to cancel all other unrelated loans of the debtor
explanation: Under Section 140 of the Indian Contract Act, where a guaranteed debt has become due and default of payment has been made, the surety, upon paying or performing what he is liable for, is invested with all the rights which the creditor had against the principal debtor (Right of Subrogation).

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: If a corporate borrower issues a balance sheet containing a specific entry acknowledging its debt to a bank, how does Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963 apply to this balance sheet acknowledgment?
audio_script: If a corporate borrower issues a balance sheet containing a specific entry acknowledging its debt to a bank, how does Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963 apply to this balance sheet acknowledgment?
option_a: Balance sheets are statutory documents and can never qualify as an acknowledgment under Section 18.
option_b: It qualifies as a valid acknowledgment in writing under Section 18, provided the balance sheet is signed by authorized directors or personnel, extending the limitation period.
option_c: It automatically extends limitation by 12 years regardless of whether it is signed or not.
option_d: It only extends limitation if approved by the Reserve Bank of India.
explanation: Judicial precedents under Section 18 of the Limitation Act establish that a balance sheet signed by the company's directors or authorized signatories acknowledging a debt constitutes a valid acknowledgment of liability, thereby computing a fresh period of limitation from the date of the balance sheet.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: When a borrower faces temporary genuine hardship, what regulatory-compliant resolution mechanism is typically offered by banks instead of immediate legal action?
audio_script: When a borrower faces temporary genuine hardship, what regulatory-compliant resolution mechanism is typically offered by banks instead of immediate legal action?
option_a: Immediate attachment of all personal assets without notice
option_b: Debt restructuring involving tenure extension or rate modification
option_c: Public shaming through local newspaper advertisements
option_d: Filing a criminal complaint for civil defaults
explanation: Debt restructuring, such as extending the loan tenure or revising EMI structures, is designed to support borrowers facing temporary genuine hardship.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: When a bank extends credit facilities against a hypothecation deed of movable assets (such as book debts and inventory), within what statutory timeline must the particulars of such a charge be filed with the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI) under the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
audio_script: Within what statutory timeline must the particulars of a charge by hypothecation be filed with CERSAI under the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
option_a: Within 15 days from the date of execution of the hypothecation deed, extendable by the Registrar up to 30 days
option_b: Within 30 days from the date of the creation or modification of the security interest, with provisions for condonation of delay
option_c: Within 60 days from the date of disbursement of the first tranche of the credit facility
option_d: Within 90 days from the date of classification of the account as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA)
explanation: Under Chapter IV-A of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, and relevant rules thereunder, particulars of creation, modification, or satisfaction of security interest (including hypothecation) must be filed with CERSAI within 30 days from the date of such creation or modification.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Regarding data privacy and storage under the RBI Digital Lending Guidelines, what restriction is placed on Lending Service Providers (LSPs) and Regulated Entities (REs) concerning borrower data?
audio_script: Regarding data privacy and storage under the RBI Digital Lending Guidelines, what restriction is placed on Lending Service Providers and Regulated Entities concerning borrower data?
option_a: REs must ensure that LSPs store all borrower data indefinitely on offshore servers
option_b: Any data collected by digital lending apps must be strictly need-based, with explicit consent, and without storing biometric data
option_c: LSPs are allowed to sell borrower contact lists to third-party marketers without restriction
option_d: Borrower mobile phone contact lists can be accessed unconditionally for recovery purposes
explanation: RBI guidelines require that data collection by digital lending apps must be need-based, have explicit prior consent of the borrower, and prohibit the unwarranted collection of mobile phone resources like contact lists or media files.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: In the context of escrow account arrangements mandated for FLDG structures under RBI's digital lending framework, where must the invoked FLDG amount be maintained by the Lending Service Provider (LSP), and what is the explicit mandate regarding continuous credit underwriting by the Regulated Entity (RE)?
audio_script: In the context of escrow account arrangements mandated for FLDG structures under RBI's digital lending framework, where must the invoked FLDG amount be maintained by the Lending Service Provider, and what is the explicit mandate regarding continuous credit underwriting by the Regulated Entity?
option_a: In a designated fixed deposit with the LSP's own bank; RE can outsource underwriting completely to the LSP
option_b: In a scheduled commercial bank account kept as an escrow account; RE must independently conduct credit underwriting for every borrower and cannot delegate it to the LSP
option_c: In current accounts of the RE without restriction; LSP is solely responsible for credit underwriting
option_d: In mutual fund liquid schemes managed by the LSP; RE shares underwriting responsibility equally with the LSP
explanation: RBI guidelines mandate that any FLDG invoked must be kept in a scheduled commercial bank designated as an escrow account. Crucially, the Regulated Entity (RE) cannot pass on its core credit underwriting responsibilities or make credit decisions based solely on the LSP's recommendations; continuous credit underwriting remains the explicit obligation of the RE.

question_text: Under Section 14 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, a moratorium is declared upon the admission of a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP). Which of the following statements is legally accurate regarding the applicability of this moratorium to a Personal Guarantor (PG) of the Corporate Debtor (CD)?
audio_script: Under Section 14 of the IBC, 2016, a moratorium is declared upon the admission of a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process. Which of the following statements is legally accurate regarding the applicability of this moratorium to a Personal Guarantor of the Corporate Debtor?
option_a: The moratorium under Section 14 automatically stays all recovery actions and legal proceedings against the personal guarantor of the corporate debtor simultaneously.
option_b: The moratorium under Section 14 does not apply to the personal guarantor of the corporate debtor, as established by Supreme Court jurisprudence, allowing creditors to pursue recovery actions against the guarantor under the SARFAESI Act or IBC provisions independently.
option_c: The moratorium stays recovery actions against personal guarantors only if the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) passes a specific injunction order upon application by the resolution professional.
option_d: The moratorium suspends all guarantor liabilities for a fixed statutory period of 180 days, extendable by another 90 days, identical to the corporate debtor.
explanation: As clarified by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 'Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India', the approval of a resolution plan for the corporate debtor does not release or discharge the personal guarantor from their liability. Furthermore, Section 14 moratorium applies strictly to the assets of the 'Corporate Debtor' and does not extend to personal guarantors, meaning creditors can initiate or continue recovery proceedings against personal guarantors independently.

audio_script: A corporate borrower defaults on a term loan secured by hypothecation of machinery and mortgage of land. The creditor enforces security via SARFAESI Act, 2002. Which timeline correctly reflects the enforcement phase under Section 13(2) and Section 13(4)?
option_a: Issue 30 days notice under Section 13(2), followed immediately by possession under Section 13(4) if no representation is made.
option_b: Issue 60 days demand notice under Section 13(2); upon failure to pay, take measures under Section 13(4) after considering objections within 15 days.
option_c: Issue 90 days demand notice under Section 13(2), followed by a mandatory 30-day cooling period before taking symbolic possession.

explanation: Under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, the secured creditor must issue a demand notice giving the borrower 60 days to clear the dues. If the borrower makes a representation or raises an objection, the creditor must reply within 15 days of receiving such representation, rejecting or accepting it, before proceeding with measures under Section 13(4).

question_text: A registered partnership firm defaults on a cash credit facility availed from a bank. One of the partners retires without giving public notice of retirement under Section 72 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, and the firm becomes insolvent subsequently. As per Section 45, what is the extent of liability of this retired partner for the firm's debts incurred *prior* to their retirement, vis-a-vis the bank's recovery proceedings?
audio_script: A registered partnership firm defaults on a cash credit facility. One partner retires without giving public notice under Section 72, and the firm later becomes insolvent. Under Section 45, what is the liability of this retired partner for debts incurred before retirement?
option_a: The retired partner is completely absolved of all liabilities the moment they execute the retirement deed inter se.
option_b: The retired partner remains liable to the bank for acts done before retirement because no public notice was given as mandated by Section 45 and Section 72.
option_c: The retired partner's liability is automatically extinguished upon the insolvency of the firm, transferring all debts to the official assignee.
option_d: The retired partner is liable only if the bank specifically obtained a personal guarantee from them at the time of sanctioning the credit facility.
explanation: Under Section 45 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, partners continue to be liable to third parties for any act done by any of them which would have been an act of the firm if done before the public notice, until public notice is given of the retirement. Section 72 mandates public notice in the Official Gazette and vernacular newspapers. Therefore, failing to give public notice keeps the retired partner liable to the bank for pre-retirement debts.

The firm wants to file a suit for recovery against the third-party debtor in a civil court. Referring to Section 69 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, what is the legal status of this recovery suit?
option_a: The suit is fully maintainable because Section 69 bars suits only between partners and not against third parties.
option_b: The suit is barred because Section 69(1) prohibits any suit to enforce a right arising from a contract by or on behalf of an unregistered firm against a third party.
option_c: The suit is maintainable only if the Debt Recovery Tribunal grants special permission.
option_d: The suit is maintainable provided the loan amount does not exceed Rs. 10,00,000.

Since M/s Apex Traders is unregistered, the recovery suit against the third-party debtor is barred.

question_text: How does a 'Pledge' (governed by Sections 172 to 182 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872) fundamentally differ from a 'Hypothecation' in terms of legal possession and control of the security?
audio_script: How does a Pledge fundamentally differ from a Hypothecation in terms of legal possession and control of the security?
option_a: In a pledge, constructive possession remains with the borrower, while in hypothecation, physical possession is transferred to the bank.
option_b: In a pledge, actual or constructive delivery of goods is a prerequisite, whereas in hypothecation, both ownership and physical possession remain with the borrower with only a charge created.
option_c: Hypothecation applies strictly to immovable assets, whereas pledge applies solely to actionable claims.
option_d: Neither involves any transfer of possession, but pledge requires compulsory registration under the Companies Act.
explanation: A pledge requires the bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt, entailing the transfer of actual or constructive possession to the pawnee. Conversely, hypothecation is a charge created over movable property without the transfer of either ownership or possession to the creation of the lender.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework

audio_script: Under the Limitation Act, 1963, what is the standard limitation period for filing a recovery suit for money lent or due under a simple contract, and from which specific date does this period begin to run?

option_b: 3 years from the date when the loan is made or when the money becomes payable
option_c: 30 years from the date of loan disbursement
option_d: 12 years from the date of demand notice
explanation: According to Article 19 and Article 21 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the limitation period for suits to recover money lent or due on a simple contract is 3 years, and time begins to run from the date when the loan is made or when the debt becomes due/payable.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a 'margin requirement' by banks while financing against collateral securities?
audio_script: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a margin requirement by banks while financing against collateral securities?
option_a: To increase the interest rate charged to the borrower
option_b: To cover potential depreciation in the market value of the security and cover default risk
option_c: To pay the processing fees to the Reserve Bank of India
option_d: To ensure the borrower opens a current account with the bank
explanation: Margin is the difference between the market value of the security offered and the loan amount sanctioned. It provides a cushion to the bank against a drop in the market value of the security and covers default risk.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics

option_a: Immediate criminal prosecution of the bank's Board of Directors under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.
option_b: Levying of monetary penalties on the bank and advising the bank to ban the concerned recovery agency from undertaking any recovery assignments.
option_c: Mandatory conversion of all retail loan portfolios into zero-interest accounts for a period of one financial year.
option_d: Immediate revocation of the bank's operational banking license without serving a show-cause notice.
explanation: Banks are ultimately responsible for the actions of their outsourced recovery agents. RBI can penalize banks for outsourcing violations and direct them to blacklist agencies that employ unethical recovery practices.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Which of the following requirements is essential for a payment of interest or principal to qualify for extending limitation under Section 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963?
audio_script: Which of the following requirements is essential for a payment of interest or principal to qualify for extending limitation under Section 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963?
option_a: The payment must appear in the handwriting of, or in a writing signed by, the person making the payment.
option_b: The payment must be made strictly through cash deposit at the bank branch.
option_c: The payment must cover the entire outstanding accumulated interest.
option_d: The payment must be endorsed by the Reserve Bank of India.
explanation: Section 19 requires that save in the case of a payment of interest made before the 1st day of January, 1928, an acknowledgement of the payment must appear in the handwriting of, or in a writing signed by, the person making the payment to extend the limitation period.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: [CBT-19-Item06] Under Section 143A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, what is the maximum percentage of the cheque amount that a Court can direct the drawer to pay as Interim Compensation?

option_a: Not exceeding 20% of the amount of the dishonoured cheque
option_b: Not exceeding 50% of the total claim value
option_c: Not exceeding 10% subject to approval by the Sessions Court
option_d: Not exceeding 100% of the unpaid loan principal
explanation: Section 143A empowers the Court trying a Section 138 complaint to order the drawer to pay interim compensation up to a maximum of 20% of the cheque amount.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives

audio_script: Under the digital lending directions, if a borrower wishes to exit a digital loan by paying the principal and proportionate APR, what is the mandatory cooling-off period that Regulated Entities must provide?
option_a: 1 to 3 days
option_b: A period determined by the RE, ranging between 3 to 7 days
option_c: 30 days
option_d: No cooling-off period is required for digital loans
explanation: RBI mandates a cooling-off/look-up period during which the borrower can exit digital loans without penalty, the duration of which is determined by the RE's board but must be a minimum specified timeframe (typically standardized across REs).

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: According to the RBI Fair Practices Code for Lenders and guidelines on recovery agents, during what specific time window are agents permitted to contact borrowers for recovery purposes?
audio_script: According to the RBI Fair Practices Code for Lenders and guidelines on recovery agents, during what specific time window are agents permitted to contact borrowers for recovery purposes?
explanation: RBI guidelines strictly mandate that recovery agents and lenders can contact borrowers only between 08:00 AM and 07:00 PM to protect borrowers' privacy and prevent undue harassment.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities

audio_script: Under RBI guidelines regarding the assessment of working capital, the Maximum Permissible Bank Finance MPBF under the Second Method of Lending recommended by the Tandon Committee requires that the borrower must finance what percentage of current assets from long term funds Net Working Capital?
option_a: Minimum 15 percent
option_b: Minimum 25 percent
option_c: Minimum 40 percent
option_d: Minimum 50 percent
explanation: Under the Second Method of Lending of the Tandon Committee, the borrower's contribution to working capital (Net Working Capital) must be at least 25 percent of the total current assets, and the bank finance covers the remaining 75 percent.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Under Section 25 of the PSS Act, 2007, what legal presumption does the court draw regarding the holder of the electronic fund transfer receiving it for the discharge of any debt or other liability, unless the contrary is proved?
audio_script: Under Section 25 of the PSS Act, 2007, what legal presumption does the court draw regarding the holder of the electronic fund transfer receiving it for the discharge of any debt or other liability, unless the contrary is proved?
option_a: No presumption exists; the complainant must prove absolute commercial intent
option_b: It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the electronic fund transfer was received for the discharge of, in whole or in part, any debt or other liability
option_c: It is presumed that the mandate was executed under duress
option_d: The bank takes joint liability for the dishonoured mandate
explanation: Section 25(2) of the PSS Act, 2007 establishes a rebuttable presumption that the electronic funds transfer was received for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, similar to Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: When differentiating between a Term Loan and Working Capital Finance, which of the following core lending principles is primarily addressed through the sanction of a Term Loan?
audio_script: When differentiating between a Term Loan and Working Capital Finance, which of the following core lending principles is primarily addressed through the sanction of a Term Loan?
option_a: Liquidity
option_b: Profitability
option_c: Safety through creation of fixed assets and matching cash flows
option_d: Immediate cash conversion cycle management
explanation: Term loans are granted for the acquisition of fixed assets and are repaid out of the future cash generations over a medium to long-term period, thereby addressing the principle of safety and matching the repayment source with cash flows.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: [CBT-19-Item07] What is the statutory timeline for filing an appeal before the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT) against an order of the DRT under Section 20 of the RDB Act, 1993?

option_a: Within 30 days from the date of receipt of the DRT order, accompanied by mandatory pre-deposit

option_d: Within 90 days following the publication of the final recovery certificate
explanation: Section 20 of the RDB Act prescribes a 30-day timeline to file an appeal before the DRAT, subject to mandatory pre-deposit of 50% (relaxable to not less than 25%).

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963 deals with the effect of acknowledgment of liability in writing. For such an acknowledgment to extend the limitation period afresh, what essential statutory condition must be met regarding its timing and form?
audio_script: Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963 deals with the effect of acknowledgment of liability in writing. For such an acknowledgment to extend the limitation period afresh, what essential statutory condition must be met regarding its timing and form?
option_a: It must be signed orally before witnesses after the limitation period has expired.
option_b: It must be in writing, signed by the party against whom the property or right is claimed, and made before the expiration of the prescribed limitation period.
option_c: It must be registered as a deed before a sub-registrar within 30 days of execution.
option_d: It must be executed exclusively by a court-appointed receiver.
explanation: Section 18 requires that an acknowledgment of liability must be in writing and signed by the party concerned (or their authorized agent) before the expiration of the prescribed period of limitation for that suit or application.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: Which of the following is considered a case of 'genuine hardship' rather than a willful default during borrower assessment?

option_b: Deliberate diversion of funds to acquire personal luxury assets
option_c: Refusal to pay despite having adequate liquid funds and income sources
option_d: Siphoning off business revenues to shell companies
explanation: Sudden medical emergencies or unexpected job losses impairing repayment capacity are classic examples of genuine financial distress, distinct from willful default.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: [CBT-19-Item08] Under RBI guidelines on Fair Practices Code, what is the strict restriction regarding visiting or contacting borrowers at their place of employment/workplace?

option_a: Agents must not visit or call borrowers at work unless specifically requested or consented to by the borrower

option_c: Agents may discuss the borrower's default with coworkers to apply peer recovery pressure
option_d: Agents can request the employer to withhold 50% of the borrower's monthly remuneration directly
explanation: RBI guidelines explicitly prohibit agents from visiting or contacting a borrower at their workplace without prior consent, and strictly prohibit disclosing debt details to colleagues.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: [CBT-19-Item09] Under the IIBF Code of Ethics for Recovery Agents, what must an agent explicitly display to a borrower before commencing any debt recovery communication?

option_d: A complete loan statement showing other defaulting borrowers in the district
explanation: An agent must display an authentic Identity Card and the bank's written Authorisation Letter before initiating any recovery dialogue.

explanation: Regulatory and internal bank margins act as a cushion against adverse fluctuations in the market value of securities, ensuring that the bank's exposure remains fully covered even if asset prices drop.

option_a: Both possession and ownership are transferred to the bank

explanation: Hypothecation is a charge created on movable property where neither ownership nor possession is passed to the lender; the borrower retains both, but the lender gets an equitable charge.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: According to Section 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963, where payment on account of a debt is made before the expiration of the prescribed period by the borrower's agent, what is the mandatory requirement for such part-payment to extend the limitation period, and from when does the fresh limitation period compute?
audio_script: According to Section 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963, where payment on account of a debt is made before the expiration of the prescribed period by the borrower's agent, what is the mandatory requirement for such part-payment to extend the limitation period, and from when does the fresh limitation period compute?
option_a: The payment must be in cash only, and limitation computes from the date the loan was originally sanctioned.
option_b: The payment must be evidenced by a writing signed in the hand of, or by an agent duly authorized in this behalf by, the person liable, and the fresh limitation computes from the time when the payment was made.
option_c: The payment must be notified to the court, and limitation computes from the date of default notice.
option_d: No written acknowledgement is required for part-payment, and limitation automatically extends by 12 years from the date of payment.
explanation: Section 19 of the Limitation Act mandates that where payment on account of a debt is made before the expiration of the prescribed period by the person liable or their duly authorized agent, the fact of such payment must appear in a writing signed by or on behalf of the person making it. A fresh period of limitation is computed from the time when the payment was made.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework

option_c: C
option_d: The NDNC registry applies strictly to promotional marketing calls and does not exempt financial recovery calls.
explanation: While transactional or service calls related to existing accounts have specific exemptions under telecom regulations, RBI and TRAI guidelines require adherence to customer preferences, and calls can be made if the borrower has consented or when contacting for verified debt recovery within permitted hours, though explicit contractual consent or specific statutory exemptions apply. However, under strict regulatory frameworks, explicit consent in loan documentation overrides general NDNC restrictions for genuine default follow-ups.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Can a Lok Adalat decide a matter on merits if a settlement or compromise is not reached between the bank and the borrower?
audio_script: Can a Lok Adalat decide a matter on merits if a settlement or compromise is not reached between the bank and the borrower?
option_a: Yes, it can pass a binding summary judgment on merits
option_b: No, if the parties do not arrive at a compromise, the Lok Adalat has no jurisdiction to decide on merits and must return the case to the referring court
option_c: Yes, with the written consent of only the financial institution
option_d: No, but it can refer the matter directly to the Supreme Court
explanation: Lok Adalats derive their authority from consensual settlement. If no compromise is reached, the Lok Adalat has no adjudicatory power on merits and must return the record of the case to the court from which it was received.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: As per the guidelines governing debt recovery agents, how must details of visits made to borrowers' premises be officially logged by the recovery agency?
audio_script: As per the guidelines governing debt recovery agents, how must details of visits made to borrowers' premises be officially logged by the recovery agency?
option_a: Details must be recorded in a digital spreadsheet shared weekly via personal messaging apps.
option_b: Details must be maintained and recorded chronologically in a daily register maintained by the agency.
option_c: Logging visits is optional as long as telephonic contact logs are maintained.
option_d: Details must be submitted directly to the local police station before undertaking any home visit.
explanation: Recovery agencies are required to maintain a daily register recording all visits made by their agents to borrowers' premises, ensuring accountability and compliance with regulatory standards.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: According to the IBA Model Code of Conduct for Direct Sales Agents (DSAs) and Recovery Agents, which specific mandatory protocol must be followed immediately upon approaching a defaulting borrower or guarantor during a home visit?
audio_script: According to the IBA Model Code of Conduct for Direct Sales Agents and Recovery Agents, which specific mandatory protocol must be followed immediately upon approaching a defaulting borrower or guarantor during a home visit?
option_a: Obtain written permission from the local police station before entering the residential premises.
option_b: Display identity cards issued by the bank or the agency along with the authorization letter from the bank.
option_c: Serve a formal printed demand notice carrying the wet signature of the bank's Chief Executive Officer.
option_d: Record the entire interaction on a digital video device to serve as evidentiary proof of the visit.
explanation: As per the IBA Model Code of Conduct, recovery agents must invariably display their identity cards issued by the bank/agency along with an authorization letter from the bank upon making contact with the customer.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: [CBT-19-Item12] Under RBI Master Directions, what are the statutory eligibility thresholds for an NBFC to enforce security interests under the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
audio_script: Question 12. Under RBI Master Directions, what are the statutory eligibility thresholds for an NBFC to enforce security interests under the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
option_a: Asset size of Rs 100 Crore and above, with a minimum default claim threshold of Rs 20 Lakh
option_b: Asset size of Rs 500 Crore and above, with a minimum default claim threshold of Rs 1 Crore
option_c: Asset size of Rs 50 Crore and above, with a minimum default claim threshold of Rs 5 Lakh
option_d: Asset size of Rs 1,000 Crore with zero net Non-Performing Assets
explanation: NBFCs with an asset size of Rs 100 Crore and above are notified as financial institutions under the SARFAESI Act with a minimum debt enforcement threshold of Rs 20 Lakh.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: In the context of the IBA Model Code regarding visit logs and documentation during recovery procedures, what is the mandatory protocol a DRA must follow immediately after completing a field visit to a borrower's premises?
audio_script: In the context of the IBA Model Code regarding visit logs and documentation during recovery procedures, what is the mandatory protocol a DRA must follow immediately after completing a field visit to a borrower's premises?
option_a: Submit a verbal report to the collection manager over the phone within 48 hours
option_b: Maintain a detailed visit log recording the exact time, date, persons met, and outcome, and ensure contemporaneous reporting to the bank's system
option_c: Destroy all field notes to maintain borrower privacy under data protection norms
option_d: Publish the visit outcome on the public notice board of the local police station
explanation: Under the IBA guidelines and fair practices code, DRAs are required to maintain a precise and contemporaneous visit log detailing all interactions, timestamps, and discussions during field visits, which must be immediately updated and accessible to the lending bank for audit and compliance tracking.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: [CBT-19-Item13] Under Section 171 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, in which of the following cases can a bank NOT exercise its statutory General Lien?
audio_script: Question 13. Under Section 171 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, in which of the following cases can a bank NOT exercise its statutory General Lien?
option_a: On gold ornaments or securities left expressly for safe custody or for an ear-marked trust purpose
option_b: On proceeds of credit bills deposited for general collection without restrictions
option_c: On surplus proceeds remaining after the sale of an earlier pledged security
option_d: On mature fixed deposits standing in the borrower's own individual name
explanation: A banker's general lien applies strictly to securities bailed in the ordinary course of business. Valuables left specifically for safe custody or dedicated trust purposes are exempt from lien.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: In the context of banking loans, if a guarantor signs a guarantee deed, what term is used under Section 126 for the person to whom the guarantee is given?
audio_script: In the context of banking loans, if a guarantor signs a guarantee deed, what term is used under Section 126 for the person to whom the guarantee is given?
option_a: Surety
option_b: Principal Debtor
option_c: Creditor
option_d: Indemnifier
explanation: Under Section 126, the person to whom the guarantee is given (such as a bank lending money) is termed the 'creditor', and the person giving the guarantee is the 'surety'.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: In a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) governed by Mitakshara law, the Karta executes a mortgage of ancestral property to secure a business loan without the consent of minor coparceners. Subsequently, a total partition of the HUF takes place. In a recovery suit filed by the bank against the coparceners post-partition, upon whom does the primary burden of proof lie to establish 'legal necessity' (Aghama) or benefit of the estate to bind the shares allotted to the erstwhile minor coparceners?
audio_script: In an HUF mortgage case, after a total partition, who bears the primary burden of proving legal necessity to bind the shares of erstwhile minor coparceners?
option_a: The erstwhile minor coparceners, to prove the loan was squandered for immoral purposes.
option_b: The creditor bank, to affirmatively prove that the advance was taken for legal necessity or benefit of the estate.
option_c: The Karta exclusively, in his personal capacity without involving the partitioned coparceners.
option_d: The District Court magistrate suo motu during the preliminary decree proceedings.
explanation: Under Hindu Law, when a creditor seeks to enforce a mortgage or debt executed by the Karta against ancestral property, especially involving shares of minor coparceners post-partition, the burden of proof heavily lies on the creditor (bank) to establish that the debt was contracted for legal necessity or the benefit of the family estate.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Which of the following statements is legally accurate regarding the bar of limitation under Section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1963, in the context of debt recovery suits filed by banking institutions?
audio_script: Which of the following statements is legally accurate regarding the bar of limitation under Section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1963, in the context of debt recovery suits filed by banking institutions?
option_a: Courts are bound to dismiss a suit instituted after the prescribed limitation period, even if the defendant has not specifically raised the defense of limitation in their written statement.
option_b: Limitation bars only the remedy of filing a suit, but the underlying substantive right to the debt is automatically extinguished.
option_c: Banks are completely exempt from the provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963 under special RBI banking privileges.
option_d: A debt becomes legally non-existent after 3 years, preventing any voluntary payments by the borrower.
explanation: Section 3 of the Limitation Act mandates that every suit instituted after the prescribed period of limitation shall be dismissed, even though limitation has not been set up as a defense. Furthermore, limitation bars the remedy of a legal suit, but does not extinguish the substantive right (except under specific provisions like Section 27 for property).

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: A borrower has registered their telephone number in the National Do Not Call (NDNC) registry. Under RBI directives regarding recovery agents, when is a recovery agent permitted to make unsolicited calls to this borrower?
audio_script: A borrower has registered their telephone number in the National Do Not Call registry. Under RBI directives regarding recovery agents, when is a recovery agent permitted to make unsolicited calls to this borrower?
option_a: When the loan account has crossed 90 days past due (NPA status).
option_b: When explicit written consent has been obtained from the borrower for debt collection calls.
option_c: Recovery agents are strictly prohibited from making unsolicited calls to numbers registered in the Do-Not-Call registry, regardless of loan delinquency.
option_d: Only during the permitted calling hours of 08:00 AM to 07:00 PM.
explanation: RBI directives mandate strict compliance with Do-Not-Call registry rules. Recovery agents cannot bypass the registry for collection calls unless specific regulatory exemptions apply, protecting registered consumers from unsolicited communications.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: [CBT-19-Item14] What legal principle governs the Right of Set-off exercisable by a lending institution against a customer's deposit accounts?
audio_script: Question 14. What legal principle governs the Right of Set-off exercisable by a lending institution against a customer's deposit accounts?
option_a: Mutuality of debts where claims are due to and from the same parties in the exact same legal capacity
option_b: A compulsory prior clearance certificate obtained from the local Debt Recovery Tribunal
option_c: An irrevocable court warrant issued by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate
option_d: The requirement that the customer must be declared an insolvent by a civil court
explanation: Set-off requires mutuality of debts—the debts must be between the same parties in the same legal right and capacity (e.g., individual credit cannot be set off against partnership dues).

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: Which of the following actions constitutes an unacceptable violation of the RBI guidelines regarding recovery agent communication?
audio_script: Which of the following actions constitutes an unacceptable violation of the RBI guidelines regarding recovery agent communication?
option_a: Calling the borrower at 02:00 PM to discuss payment schedules
option_b: Sending a polite reminder SMS during daytime hours
option_c: Contacting the borrower's relatives, friends, or neighbors repeatedly to humiliate or pressure the borrower
option_d: Providing official statement of accounts upon request
explanation: Contacting family members, friends, or neighbors of the borrower with whom there is no privity of contract, especially for shaming or coercing the borrower, is a severe violation of RBI guidelines.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: According to Section 25 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, an electronic fund transfer instruction dishonor offense is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend up to how many years, or with a fine, or both?
audio_script: According to Section 25 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, an electronic fund transfer instruction dishonor offense is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend up to how many years, or with a fine, or both?
option_a: One year
option_b: Two years
option_c: Five years
option_d: Seven years
explanation: Section 25(1) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 stipulates that the punishment for dishonor of electronic funds transfer instructions can extend up to two years of imprisonment, or with a fine up to twice the amount of the electronic funds transfer, or with both.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: [CBT-19-Item15] When a bank branch receives a Garnishee Order Nisi issued under Order XXI Rule 46 of the Civil Procedure Code, what specific funds are attached?
audio_script: Question 15. When a bank branch receives a Garnishee Order Nisi issued under Order XXI Rule 46 of the Civil Procedure Code, what specific funds are attached?
option_a: Only the cleared credit balance due or accruing due at the exact moment the order is served on the bank
option_b: All future salary credits and remittances credited to the account over the subsequent 6 months
option_c: Uncleared cheques and bills deposited for collection that have not yet been realized
option_d: All independent accounts belonging to the customer's immediate blood relatives
explanation: A Garnishee Order Nisi attaches only the debts due or accruing due at the time of service. It does not attach future credits or uncleared cheques.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: While evaluating the principles of good lending, which of the following best defines the concept of 'Margin' maintained by a bank against securities charged?
audio_script: While evaluating the principles of good lending, which of the following best defines the concept of Margin maintained by a bank against securities charged?
option_a: The profit margin charged by the borrower on goods sold against bank finance.
option_b: The difference between the market value of the security and the drawing power or loan amount granted.
option_c: The interest spread maintained by the bank between deposit rates and lending rates.
option_d: The minimum cash reserve ratio maintained with the Reserve Bank of India.
explanation: Margin represents the percentage of the market value of the security that is not financed by the bank. It is the difference between the market value of the collateral and the actual loan amount/drawing power to absorb potential price fluctuations.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Working capital loans granted by banks are primarily intended to finance which of the following requirements of a business enterprise?
audio_script: Working capital loans granted by banks are primarily intended to finance which of the following requirements of a business enterprise?
option_a: Acquisition of land and construction of factory buildings
option_b: Purchase of heavy machinery and long-term equipment
option_c: Day-to-day operational expenses like purchase of raw materials and holding inventory
option_d: Payment of long-term corporate dividends to shareholders
explanation: Working capital finance is short-term credit facility provided to meet day-to-day operational needs such as purchase of raw materials, payment of wages, and maintenance of inventory and receivables.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: What action should a recovery agent take upon meeting a borrower for the first time during a field visit, as per the mandated Fair Practices Code?

option_a: Demand immediate cash payment without documentation

option_c: Enter the premises without permission to inspect assets
option_d: Threaten legal action immediately
explanation: Recovery agents must always display their identity cards and carry an explicit authorization letter from the bank/financial institution when interacting with borrowers in the field.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: [CBT-19-Item16] Under RBI Master Directions on KYC, which among the following is categorized as an Officially Valid Document (OVD) for Proof of Identity and Address?

option_d: Utility electric bill not older than two calendar months
explanation: Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) under RBI KYC Directions include Passport, Driving Licence, Proof of Aadhaar, Voter ID, NREGA Job Card, and NPR Letter.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: How many days does the drawer of a dishonoured NACH or ECS mandate have to make payment to the payee after the receipt of the written demand notice under Section 25 of the PSS Act, 2007, before a criminal complaint can be filed?
audio_script: How many days does the drawer of a dishonoured NACH or ECS mandate have to make payment to the payee after the receipt of the written demand notice under Section 25 of the PSS Act, 2007, before a criminal complaint can be filed?
option_a: 7 days
option_b: 14 days
option_c: 15 days
option_d: 30 days
explanation: Under Section 25(1)(c) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the drawer of such electronic transfer must fail to pay the said amount of money to the payee within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice, following which the cause of action arises.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Under Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, which of the following persons can be held vicariously liable for an offense committed by a company, provided they were in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business at the material time?
audio_script: Under Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, which of the following persons can be held vicariously liable for an offense committed by a company, provided they were in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business at the material time?
option_a: Only the Managing Director and Company Secretary
option_b: Any person who is a silent investor holding more than 50% equity in the company
option_c: Every person who, at the time the offense was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as any director, manager, secretary or other officer with whose consent, connivance or attribution the offense is proved to have been committed
option_d: Independent non-executive directors who have no involvement in the day-to-day management or financial operations of the company
explanation: Section 141 of the NI Act states that every person who, at the time the offense was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, along with directors, managers, secretaries, or other officers whose consent, connivance, or neglect led to the offense, shall be deemed guilty.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Under the Motor Vehicles Act and RBI regulations governing vehicle loans, what is the mandatory requirement regarding the registration certificate (RC) of a hypothecated commercial vehicle, and what specific endorsement must be made to protect the financier's security interest?
audio_script: Under the Motor Vehicles Act and RBI regulations governing vehicle loans, what is the mandatory requirement regarding the registration certificate of a hypothecated commercial vehicle, and what specific endorsement must be made to protect the financier's security interest?
option_a: The RC must be retained by the borrower, and the financier's name must be endorsed as 'Lessor' in the certificate.
option_b: The RC must be deposited with the Regional Transport Office (RTO) with an endorsement of hypothecation in favor of the bank under Section 51 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
option_c: The RC must reflect the bank as the registered owner, and the financier must hold the original physical copy at all times.
option_d: Hypothecation endorsement is optional for commercial vehicles if a separate charge is registered with the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI).
explanation: As per Section 51 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, when a vehicle is subject to a hypothecation agreement, the application for registration must include an entry of the hypothecation agreement in favor of the financier, and the RTO makes an endorsement reflecting the same on the Registration Certificate (RC).

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: When extending credit facilities to a Sole Proprietorship concern, what is the fundamental legal nature of the proprietor's liability for business debts in relation to personal assets?
audio_script: When extending credit facilities to a Sole Proprietorship concern, what is the fundamental legal nature of the proprietor's liability for business debts in relation to personal assets?
option_a: The proprietor's liability is strictly limited to the capital invested in the sole proprietorship business.
option_b: The proprietor and the sole proprietorship are legally distinct entities, shielding personal assets from business recovery actions.
option_c: The proprietor has unlimited personal liability, meaning personal assets can be attached and sold to satisfy business debts.
option_d: Personal assets can only be attached if explicitly mortgaged under a separate individual loan agreement.
explanation: A sole proprietorship has no separate legal identity distinct from its owner. Therefore, the sole proprietor has unlimited personal liability, and all personal assets can be attached and proceeded against by Debt Recovery Agents or banks to recover business dues.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: As per RBI guidelines and the Code of Conduct for Debt Recovery Agents, for what minimum duration must a Recovery Agent or Bank preserve call recordings and communication logs related to customer recovery interactions?
audio_script: As per RBI guidelines and the Code of Conduct for Debt Recovery Agents, for what minimum duration must a Recovery Agent or Bank preserve call recordings and communication logs related to customer recovery interactions?
option_a: 3 months
option_b: 6 months
option_c: 1 year
option_d: 3 years
explanation: According to regulatory standards and fair practices codes governing recovery agents, all call recordings and logs of communication with borrowers must be preserved for a minimum period of 6 months to address any grievances or disputes.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: Which regulatory framework governs the restriction of unsolicited commercial communications and forms the basis for respecting the 'Do-Not-Call' registry during recovery operations?
audio_script: Which regulatory framework governs the restriction of unsolicited commercial communications and forms the basis for respecting the Do-Not-Call registry during recovery operations?
option_a: Information Technology Act, 2000
option_b: Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations (TCCCPR) issued by TRAI
option_c: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Section 45ZA)
option_d: SARFAESI Act, 2002 (Section 13(4))
explanation: The Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations (TCCCPR) issued by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) governs the National Do Not Call (NDNC) registry, which financial institutions and recovery agents must respect.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: In the context of creation of charges, how does a 'Pledge' under Section 172 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, fundamentally differ from 'Hypothecation'?
audio_script: In the context of creation of charges, how does a Pledge under Section 172 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, fundamentally differ from Hypothecation?
option_a: Pledge involves the transfer of both ownership and physical possession of goods, whereas hypothecation involves only ownership transfer.
option_b: Pledge involves the bailment of goods where actual or constructive possession is transferred to the pawnee, whereas in hypothecation, both ownership and possession remain with the borrower.
option_c: Pledge is governed by the Transfer of Property Act, whereas hypothecation is governed by the Companies Act.
option_d: Pledge does not give the lender any right to sell the goods without court intervention, whereas hypothecation allows immediate sale without notice.
explanation: Under Section 172 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a pledge is the bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt, requiring the transfer of actual or constructive possession to the pawnee (lender). Hypothecation, recognized under judicial interpretation and statutes like the SARFAESI Act, involves creating a charge over movable property where both ownership and physical possession remain with the borrower.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Which statutory document serves as the primary legal evidence of creation of a security interest (hypothecation) in the case of a vehicle loan?
audio_script: Which statutory document serves as the primary legal evidence of creation of a security interest hypothecation in the case of a vehicle loan?
option_a: Deed of Mortgage
option_b: Hypothecation Agreement and CERSAI registration
option_c: Letter of Pledge
option_d: Trust Receipt
explanation: For movable assets like vehicles, security is created via a Hypothecation Agreement under the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act, 2002, and must be registered with the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI).

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Under the RBI guidelines on Digital Lending, what is the mandatory explicit 'cooling-off' or 'look-up' period during which a borroweret can repay the principal and proportionate APR without any penalty, and what condition applies to borrowers of digital loans with a tenor of less than 7 days?
audio_script: Under the RBI guidelines on Digital Lending, what is the mandatory explicit cooling-off or look-up period during which a borrower can repay the principal and proportionate APR without any penalty, and what condition applies to borrowers of digital loans with a tenor of less than 7 days?
option_a: 3 days; cooling-off period is waived entirely for loans under 7 days
option_b: 7 days; the cooling-off period is not applicable for loans with a tenor of less than 7 days
option_c: 14 days; a proportionate daily penalty is charged during the cooling-off period
option_d: 7 days; penalty is capped at 1% of the principal amount
explanation: According to RBI Digital Lending guidelines, Regulated Entities must provide an explicit cooling-off/look-up period (not less than 7 days for loans with tenor of 7 days or more, and not applicable for loans with tenor less than 7 days) during which borrowers can exit digital loans by paying the principal and proportionate APR without penalty.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: When electronic fund transfer instructions like NACH or ECS fail due to insufficient funds, the legal provisions governing the penal consequences are comparable to the dishonour of which traditional instrument under the Negotiable Instruments Act?
audio_script: When electronic fund transfer instructions like NACH or ECS fail due to insufficient funds, the legal provisions governing the penal consequences are comparable to the dishonour of which traditional instrument under the Negotiable Instruments Act?
option_a: Promissory Note
option_b: Cheque
option_c: Bill of Exchange
option_d: Letter of Credit
explanation: Section 25 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 was enacted to give electronic fund transfers and NACH/ECS transactions the same legal footing and penal consequences as cheque bounces under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: Which of the following actions is expressly PROHIBITED during the moratorium period declared under Section 14 of the IBC, 2016?
audio_script: Which of the following actions is expressly prohibited during the moratorium period declared under Section 14 of the IBC, 2016?
option_a: Supply of essential goods or services to the corporate debtor
option_b: Institution of suits or continuation of pending proceedings against the corporate debtor
option_c: Filing of income tax returns by the corporate debtor
option_d: Execution of orders passed by regulatory authorities prior to the insolvency commencement date
explanation: Section 14(1)(a) prohibits the institution of suits or continuation of pending suits or proceedings against the corporate debtor, including execution of any judgment, decree or order in any court of law, tribunal, arbitration panel or other authority.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Which entities are categorized as 'Regulated Entities' (REs) permitted to undertake digital lending under the specific RBI framework?
audio_script: Which entities are categorized as 'Regulated Entities' (REs) permitted to undertake digital lending under the specific RBI framework?
option_a: Unregistered money lenders and fintech startups
option_b: Commercial banks, Co-operative banks, and NBFCs
option_c: Merchant payment gateways only
option_d: Only third-party loan aggregators
explanation: Regulated Entities (REs) comprise entities like commercial banks, primary (urban) co-operative banks, state co-operative banks, central co-operative banks, and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Under the Master Directions on Know Your Customer (KYC) issued by the Reserve Bank of India, if an existing customer submits a current utility bill as proof of updated address—which does not fall under the standard definition of an Officially Valid Document (OVD)—within what mandatory timeframe must the customer submit an official OVD containing the updated address to prevent account freezing?
audio_script: Under the RBI KYC Master Directions, if a customer provides a utility bill as proof of an updated address, within what mandatory timeframe must they submit an official OVD containing the updated address?
option_a: Within 1 month of submitting the utility bill
option_b: Within 3 months of submitting the utility bill
option_c: Within 6 months of submitting the utility bill
option_d: Within 12 months of submitting the utility bill
explanation: As per RBI KYC guidelines, if the OVD submitted by a customer does not contain the updated address, the institution may accept a deemed OVD (such as utility bills, municipal tax receipts, etc.) for the updated address. However, the customer must submit an OVD updated with the current address within a period of 3 months from the date of submission of the deemed OVD.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: As per RBI instructions, periodic updating of KYC for low-risk individual customers is required to be carried out at least once in how many years?
audio_script: As per RBI instructions, periodic updating of KYC for low-risk individual customers is required to be carried out at least once in how many years?
option_a: Every 1 year
option_b: Every 2 years
option_c: Every 5 years
option_d: Every 10 years
explanation: According to RBI KYC directions, periodic updating of KYC for low-risk customers is required at least once every 10 years, for medium-risk customers every 8 years, and for high-risk customers every 2 years.

module: Module B: Legal & Regulatory Framework
question_text: A creditor, without the consent of the surety, enters into a binding contract with the principal debtor to give him an extra 6 months to pay the debt (time-extension). According to Section 135 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, what is the impact on the surety?
audio_script: A creditor, without the consent of the surety, enters into a binding contract with the principal debtor to give him an extra 6 months to pay the debt. According to Section 135 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, what is the impact on the surety?
option_a: The surety is discharged from liability.
option_b: The surety's liability is postponed by 6 months.
option_c: The surety remains liable immediately upon the original due date.
option_d: The surety is discharged only if the principal debtor becomes insolvent during the 6 months.
explanation: Under Section 135 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract between the creditor and the principal debtor, by which the creditor makes a composition with, or promises to give time to, or not to sue, the principal debtor, without the consent of the surety, discharges the surety.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Which statutory authority in India administers and enforces the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002?
audio_script: Which statutory authority in India administers and enforces the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002?
option_a: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
option_b: Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND)
option_c: Enforcement Directorate (ED)
option_d: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI)
explanation: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Ministry of Finance investigates and enforces offenses under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Under the current statutory provisions of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, what is the minimum asset size required for a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) to be notified by the Central Government to exercise the enforcement of security interest powers, along with the minimum default claim threshold against the borrower?
audio_script: Under the current statutory provisions of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, what is the minimum asset size required for a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) to be notified by the Central Government to exercise the enforcement of security interest powers, along with the minimum default claim threshold against the borrower?
option_a: Minimum asset size of Rs 500 Crore and minimum default claim of Rs 1 Crore
option_b: Minimum asset size of Rs 100 Crore and minimum default claim of Rs 20 Lakhs

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: An NBFC-Investment and Credit Company (NBFC-ICC) operating in the Base Layer transitions to the Middle Layer due to asset-size threshold crossing of Rs. 1,000 crore. Within how many days must the entity ensure compliance with the enhanced Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) of 15% as per RBI SBR guidelines?
audio_script: When an NBFC transitions from the Base Layer to the Middle Layer, within how many days must it comply with the enhanced 15% CRAR requirement?
option_a: 30 days from the date of audited financial statement publication
option_b: 90 days from the date of intimation by the RBI or crossing the threshold
option_c: 180 days from the date of breaching the threshold, subject to submission of a glide path
option_d: 365 days from the close of the financial year in which the threshold was breached
explanation: As per RBI Scale Based Regulation (SBR) master directions, when an NBFC moves from the Base Layer to the Middle Layer, it is allowed a transition period of up to 180 days to meet the enhanced regulatory requirements such as the 15% CRAR, provided a structured glide path is submitted and approved by the Reserve Bank of India.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: Why is the issuance of mandatory official bank receipts considered a critical compliance measure for Debt Recovery Agents (DRAs) under regulatory frameworks?
audio_script: Why is the issuance of mandatory official bank receipts considered a critical compliance measure for Debt Recovery Agents (DRAs) under regulatory frameworks?
option_a: It serves as legal proof of payment, protects the borrower against fraudulent claims of default, and ensures accountability of collected funds to the bank.
option_b: It allows the DRA to claim a higher commission percentage directly from the borrower's payment.
option_c: It exempts the lending bank from auditing the agent's daily collection ledger.
option_d: It permits the DRA to adjust collection fees directly from the cash received before depositing it.
explanation: Official bank receipts provide legally verifiable proof of payment to the borrower, safeguard against fraud, and establish a clear audit trail for funds remitted to the lending institution.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Under the legal principle derived from Clayton's Case regarding a running current account with continuous debits and credits, how are subsequent deposits traditionally applied to prior debts?
audio_script: Under the legal principle derived from Clayton's Case regarding a running current account with continuous debits and credits, how are subsequent deposits traditionally applied to prior debts?
option_a: The latest deposits are appropriated towards the newest debits
option_b: The earliest payment by way of deposit is applied to extinguish the earliest debt on the account
option_c: All credits are pooled pro-rata across all outstanding debits simultaneously
option_d: Deposits are strictly held in suspense until the account is formally closed by the bank
explanation: The Rule in Clayton's Case establishes that in a running account, the first debit item is offset by the first credit item ('first in, first out'), meaning earlier withdrawals are deemed repaid by earlier deposits.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: Under the RBI Fair Practices Code, when a borrower registers a formal grievance regarding inappropriate recovery tactics or calls made outside permitted hours, within how many days must the lender's grievance redressal mechanism resolve the issue?
audio_script: Under the RBI Fair Practices Code, when a borrower registers a formal grievance regarding inappropriate recovery tactics or calls made outside permitted hours, within how many days must the lenders grievance redressal mechanism resolve the issue?
option_a: 7 days
option_b: 15 days
option_c: 30 days
option_d: 45 days
explanation: As per RBI's general grievance redressal norms applicable to regulated entities, complaints lodged by customers including those concerning recovery agents should be dealt with and resolved promptly, typically within a maximum period of 30 days.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Regarding mobile device data access by Regulated Entities and their Lending Service Providers in digital lending, what is the stance of RBI guidelines concerning mobile data?

option_a: LSPs are permitted to access external storage files for credit scoring purposes.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: [CBT-20-Item01] As per RBI Master Directions on KYC, what is the mandatory periodic updation (re-KYC) requirement for accounts categorized under 'High Risk'?
audio_script: Question 1. As per RBI Master Directions on KYC, what is the mandatory periodic updation (re-KYC) requirement for accounts categorized under 'High Risk'?
option_a: At least once every 2 years
option_b: At least once every 5 years
option_c: At least once every 8 years
option_d: At least once every 10 years
explanation: Periodic re-KYC must be conducted at least once every 2 years for high risk, 8 years for medium risk, and 10 years for low risk accounts.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: [CBT-20-Item02] In the case of a contract entered into with a Minor for a recovery loan, what is the fundamental legal status under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Mohori Bibee precedent)?
audio_script: Question 2. In the case of a contract entered into with a Minor for a recovery loan, what is the fundamental legal status under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Mohori Bibee precedent)?
option_a: The contract is void ab initio (void from the very beginning) and unenforceable
option_b: The contract is voidable strictly at the option of the lending bank
option_c: The contract becomes legally binding as soon as the minor attains majority
option_d: The minor's natural parents are automatically liable to liquidate the debt
explanation: As established in Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose, an agreement with a minor is void ab initio and no contractual liability or debt recovery suit can arise against a minor.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics
question_text: Under data privacy norms and ethical guidelines, sharing a defaulting borrower's financial distress details with unauthorized colleagues within the recovery agency who are not directly handling the account violates which core principle?
audio_script: Under data privacy norms and ethical guidelines, sharing a defaulting borrower's financial distress details with unauthorized colleagues within the recovery agency who are not directly handling the account violates which core principle?
option_a: Public disclosure compliance
option_b: Principle of non-disclosure and customer confidentiality
option_c: Mandatory internal cross-reporting
option_d: Collateral liquidation transparency
explanation: Customer confidentiality and the principle of non-disclosure strictly prohibit sharing sensitive borrower information with any third parties or even internal colleagues who have no official 'need to know' or direct role in managing that specific account.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities
question_text: Under standard banking norms regarding term loans, how is the assessment of the quantum of loan generally structured in relation to the borrower's cash flows?
audio_script: Under standard banking norms regarding term loans, how is the assessment of the quantum of loan generally structured in relation to the borrower's cash flows?
option_a: Based purely on the personal net worth of the guarantors without evaluating project cash flows
option_b: Based on the Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) to ensure the borrower can service interest and principal instalments
option_c: Based on the maximum permissible bank finance (MPBF) method applicable exclusively to term loans
option_d: Based on the spot market price of gold pledged on the date of disbursement
explanation: Term loans are evaluated using the Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) to ascertain whether the projected cash inflows are adequate to meet the debt servicing obligations over the repayment tenure.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: Under the Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework introduced by the RBI for NBFCs, which specific layer comprises all deposit-taking NBFCs (NBFC-D) regardless of their asset size, along with non-deposit-taking NBFCs with asset sizes of Rs. 1,000 crore and above?
audio_script: Under the Scale Based Regulation framework introduced by the RBI for NBFCs, which specific layer comprises all deposit-taking NBFCs regardless of their asset size, along with non-deposit-taking NBFCs with asset sizes of Rs. 1,000 crore and above?
option_a: Base Layer
option_b: Middle Layer
option_c: Upper Layer
option_d: Top Layer
explanation: Under RBI's Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework, the Middle Layer (ML) includes all deposit-taking NBFCs (NBFC-D), non-deposit-taking NBFCs with assets of Rs. 1,000 crore and above, and certain specific categories like standalone primary dealers, infrastructure debt funds, etc.

module: Module D: NBFCs, Digital Lending & Co-operatives
question_text: When an arbitration award is obtained under Section 84 of the MSCS Act, 2002, and the award debtor fails to comply, how can the multi-state co-operative society execute the award through the Collector as arrears of land revenue?

option_a: By filing a summary suit in the High Court having jurisdiction

option_c: By direct attachment of movable properties by the recovery agent without judicial intervention
option_d: By invoking the SARFAESI Act, 2002 directly without civil court or collector execution
explanation: Under the provisions related to execution of awards under the MSCS Act, 2002, an award under Section 84 can be executed by the Collector as if it were an arrear of land revenue, upon receiving a recovery certificate signed by the Central Registrar or any person authorized by him in writing.

module: Module C: Code of Conduct & Ethics

audio_script: What temporal restriction do RBI guidelines generally impose regarding the hours during which a Debt Recovery Agent (DRA) may contact a borrower for location verification or recovery?
option_a: Contact is permitted 24 hours a day, including late nights, provided the debt is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA).
option_b: Contact must be restricted to reasonable hours, typically between 8:00 AM and 7:00 PM, to avoid harassment and respect personal privacy.
option_c: Contact can only be made between midnight and 5:00 AM when the borrower is guaranteed to be at home.
option_d: There are no specific time restrictions as long as the DRA maintains a polite tone.
explanation: RBI guidelines on fair practices for lenders stipulate that customers should be contacted only at reasonable times (typically 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM) to prevent undue harassment and invasion of privacy.

module: Module A: General Banking & Securities

audio_script: Question 3. Under the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, what is the legal position regarding daughters as coparceners in a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)?
